# Mateusz Worotyński — Fractional CTO & Product Consultant

> Mateusz Worotyński is a fractional CTO, fractional CPO and product consultant based in Kraków, Poland, working mainly with early-stage and growing startups. He co-founded PushPushGo in 2016, grew it to 200+ enterprise clients and over a billion events per day, and took it through a majority acquisition by Warsaw Stock Exchange-listed Vercom S.A. in 2021. He now works with founders and leadership teams on two tracks — technology & architecture, and product & business. **Hourly rate: 175 PLN / hour — deliberately a startup-friendly rate**, so early-stage teams can afford senior product and technology judgement before expensive mistakes happen.

Canonical site: https://worotyns.ovh/
Service pages: https://worotyns.ovh/fractional-cto/ (technology track) and https://worotyns.ovh/product-leadership/ (product & business track)

## The three reasons startups hire him

1. **Fractional CTO** — CTO-level thinking without the full-time hire: architecture, hiring and the technical bar, build-versus-buy, vendor and cloud choices, the technical side of a raise or an acquisition. One to four days a month.
2. **Architecture & technical review** — an outside read on architecture, scaling and technical debt: what breaks first at 10×, what the debt costs in weeks per month, which risks are real, and a prioritised plan. Two to three weeks.
3. **Product & business strategy** — decisions rather than workshops: what to build, what to kill, pricing, positioning and priorities, argued against revenue with the trade-offs written down.

Typical triggers: no CTO yet and no budget for one, growth that the architecture is starting to resist, a roadmap that is a list of requests, a team that needs a more senior perspective, or one important technical/product decision that is expensive to undo.

## Services — Technology & architecture

Fractional CTO: ongoing technology leadership for founders and leadership teams — architecture decisions with the reasoning written down, roadmap and build-versus-buy calls, vendor and cloud decisions, and a technical counterpart for the board. Delivered on retainer, one to four days a month.

Architecture & scaling review: a short, blunt engagement covering where the system breaks at 10× load, data models, queues, delivery paths and failure modes, the cost of each option in money and in weeks, and a prioritised plan the engineering team can start on immediately.

Technical due diligence: independent evaluation for investors, acquirers and boards — code, infrastructure and delivery-process assessment, key-person and knowledge risk, post-acquisition integration reality check, written findings.

Engineering leadership: hiring plans, interviews and technical bar, process, code review and release cadence, mentoring the first tech lead or CTO. He has hired, led and mentored a team of up to 15 engineers.

## Services — Product & business

Product strategy & roadmap: what to build, what to kill and in what order, positioning, roadmap prioritised against revenue, and the features to refuse to build.

Pricing & monetisation: tier design and the value metric behind it, freemium/trial/commission models, margin per segment and per customer, rollout without churning the existing customer base.

Go-to-market & positioning: message and category, acquisition channels that fit the price point, sales motion for enterprise and self-serve, retention and the reason customers stay.

Fractional CPO: running the product organisation — product process, cadence and decision rights, hiring and mentoring the first PM or Head of Product, customer research and prioritisation discipline.

## How engagements run

1. **Diagnose** — a call plus a hard look at what exists (code, infrastructure, delivery, hiring plan, or funnel, pricing, churn and roadmap).
2. **Decide** — two or three options with honest trade-offs, written down so the decision outlives the meeting.
3. **Build** — he builds it himself or leads the team through it.
4. **Hand over** — documented and owned by the client's team; no dependency and no proprietary framework.

## Products founded and built

- **PushPushGo** (https://pushpushgo.com) — MarTech. Multi-channel push notification platform (web push, mobile push, onsite, pop-up, WhatsApp channels) operating at over a billion events a day on bare metal and cloud, with the image CDN peaking at around 13 Gbps. Co-founded in 2016; roles: co-founder and software developer, then CPO, then CTO for the final two years. Grew to 200+ enterprise clients and a team of up to 15 people. Clients included TUI, POLITICO, Auchan, Douglas, Hearst, Aller, Planeta Sport, Home&You, Lubimyczytać, Interia, SEISKA.FI and Suomi24. In July 2021, WSE-listed Vercom S.A. acquired a majority stake of about 70% for PLN 9.43 million, with options over the remaining shares.
- **Terapeuto** (https://terapeuto.com) — MedTech, live with paying customers. Practice-management CRM for therapy centres: week schedules built from reusable slots, patient records, billing, waitlists, rooms and branches, and analytics in one system; multi-tenant, with roles for owner, therapist and reception. Bookings arrive through a widget on the clinic's own domain instead of a marketplace that takes the patient and the commission — 0% commission per booking — and each visit's price is split between organisation and therapist by a configurable commission (percentage or fixed amount), on a four-level price hierarchy (clinic, branch, therapist, patient). Founder, CTO and CPO — designed the product end to end and runs it. Prototype built in 30 days, average feature lead time around two days. In production and QA on Fly.io: session notes, national ID numbers and patient files encrypted with a Fernet key per patient (destroying a key makes that patient's data unrecoverable), every write audit-logged in the same transaction, and one container running the app plus continuous SQLite replication to S3 with point-in-time recovery — an RPO of about 30 seconds — and a daily restore test. The product's own pricing model is not public.
- **uff.email** (https://uff.email) — AI, live with paying customers. An email-native AI assistant: it gets its own address (`name@uff.email`) and its own memory, and the work you forward to it comes back in the same thread — no app, no onboarding. Priced per assistant account at 4.99 USD/month (14.99 PLN in Poland) after a 30-day trial, billed monthly by bank transfer; one address equals one memory, with no tiers and the flat price covering normal everyday use. Self-hosted and isolated per assistant: its own container and its own encrypted volume, with no published ports; memory is a knowledge graph kept as YAML, JSONL, Markdown and a JSON vector index rather than a database, mail arrives over IMAP into a filesystem queue, and a scheduler runs reminders and background work without calling the model on every tick. Ten weeks from an empty repository to production, built by one author; each assistant's model key carries a monthly spend cap, and deployment is Ansible plus a systemd restart. Founder, CTO and CPO.
- **GetViaMsg** (https://getviamsg.wdft.ovh) — FinTech, pre-production and going to market. Session-based micro-payments for publishers: the reader's phone number is the identity and an SMS is the confirmation, so there is no card, account or registration, and the commitments gathered across a session are aggregated into one report and one settlement. The publisher (tenant) pays commission on processed volume — 10% by default, hard-capped under 20%, with thresholds by monthly volume — instead of a fee per transaction; entry from 0.25 PLN with payout the next business day, against 60 days for traditional SMS Premium. The repo family covers the whole go-to-market: a Go event-sourced backend (KurrentDB, CQRS read models in SQLite, Redis locks and a scheduled delayer, deployed on OCI via Terraform/Ansible/Nomad), a single-process Deno/SQLite "lite" build for small installs (MCP/CLI/TUI operator surface, Fly.io with Litestream point-in-time recovery), a Cloudflare Workers variant in the WDFT monorepo, plus a TypeScript SDK and web-component overlay, a WordPress plugin with server-side HMAC verification, an SMS router by keyword, an R2-backed overlay config service, integration examples, a payment tester, Observable/Litestream analytics and a GeoIP microservice. Two SMS operators, multi-cloud across Fly.io, Cloudflare and Oracle Cloud, DORA-aligned controls. Co-founder and CTO.
- **Krazeta** (https://krazeta.pl) — local media, live. A daily Kraków newspaper whose editorial team is AI: one closed edition a day with a lead story, city chronicle, business and sport sections, weather, a quote, and an audio version of the edition, published as a static site on Cloudflare Pages. Business model: one sponsor per edition, four in rotation through the end of 2026; no programmatic advertising and no reader tracking, and readers do not pay. Content and state are Markdown and YAML files in Git rather than a database or a CMS, so the editorial history is versioned and auditable. Publishing every day since 19 July 2026, well past a thousand articles, from 94 approved sources, with eight LLM reporters and Conductor workflows for gathering, editing, media and deploy driven by cron. Model cost: about 1 USD per edition, covering text, voice and images. Founder.
- **ceemes.** (https://ceemes.eu) — publishing technology, proof of concept in progress (v0.0.1). A CMS for publishers that publishes static HTML: editors lay out pages in the browser (React 19 admin built with Vite 7, Puck for layout, Tiptap for article bodies) and the result is rendered server-side to files, so readers never talk to an application server — the only JavaScript on a published page is an optional 7.6 KB island. Plugin-first core: plugins declare dependencies, are sorted topologically, carry their own migration ledger and table prefix, and can be enabled per site. Each install is one tenant on one SQLite file behind Caddy, with Hono 4 on Node 20+, Drizzle over better-sqlite3 and better-auth for sessions. No tests and no CI yet. Mateusz owns the project, the technology decisions and the delivery.

Technology stacks (as published on the site): PushPushGo — MongoDB, RabbitMQ, TypeScript. Terapeuto — Python, SQLite, Litestream, Fly.io, Docker. uff.email — Python, Docker, Ansible, Mailu, filesystem state, OpenRouter. Krazeta — Python, Conductor workflows, Eleventy, Markdown in Git, OpenRouter. GetViaMsg — Go, KurrentDB, event sourcing, Deno, SQLite, Cloudflare Workers, Terraform, Nomad. ceemes. — TypeScript, Hono, React 19, Vite, SQLite, Drizzle, plugin-first.

## AI in teams

Mateusz rolls AI into engineering and product teams, and runs AI products of his own. Tooling he works with: pi agent, paperclip, opencode, OpenRouter, local models, and a deliberate mix of frontier and non-frontier models. The focus is on agent workflows inside real delivery and research pipelines, routing each task to the cheapest model that still does the job, keeping private data on local models, and managing cost per task rather than cost per token. In his own products this shows up as Krazeta (an AI newsroom) and uff.email (a self-hosted, email-native AI assistant with a knowledge-graph memory).

## Research & development — WDFT PSA

Mateusz is a co-founder of **WDFT PSA** (https://wdft.ovh), a fintech R&D company where he drives the research agenda. Concepts are written up as open standards, prototyped, and then implemented as products. Documentation index: https://docs.wdft.ovh

- **Federated Payment Standard (FPS)** — an open standard for electronic payments that uses the banks' existing infrastructure and mobile apps (deep links, QR codes) instead of building new payment infrastructure, as a cheaper alternative to existing intermediaries. Business model: no percentage commission — a flat fee per package of transactions, designed at 5 USD per 1,000 — which enables microtransactions below 1 PLN (for example an article sold for 0.50 PLN) and brings the cost of a payment close to that of an Elixir transfer. Four parts: a registry (bank directory, verification keys, API and mobile-app manifests), an SDK that generates payment links and verifies signatures, banks and providers that execute and notify, and the implementor that creates the link and receives signed webhooks — one when the customer confirms in their banking app, one once the transfer can no longer be withdrawn. Intended for banks and payment providers first, then e-commerce, publishers and POS, including QR payments for high amounts such as furniture or vehicles. Status: specification and bank sandbox. Whitepaper: https://docs.wdft.ovh/concept-federated-payment-system
- **Session-Based Payments (SBP)** — short-lived usage sessions in which a user makes small commitments across partner sites; the operator aggregates the commitments into a single settlement, then reports and pays out to each partner. Roles: user, operator, partner, bank. Terms: session, commitment, settle, report, payment, payout. Status: implemented in Poland as GetViaMsg. Whitepaper: https://docs.wdft.ovh/concept-session-based-payment

## Security & compliance

Security and compliance are treated as part of CTO-level leadership rather than a standalone service. Experience includes DORA readiness and operational-resilience controls (built into GetViaMsg from the start), NIS2 technology risk considerations, ISO 27001 practices and evidence, security audits and vulnerability management, and encryption, access control and audit trails in practice.
